uncited: It builds on [Global Uniform Data Layout](2955-global-uniform-data-layout.md) by defining the specific memory layout for individual shape instances rather than global rendering parameters.

It differs from [Camera Uniform Layout](3619-camera-uniform-layout.md) and [Appearance Frame Uniform Layout](12147-appearance-frame-uniform-layout.md) by focusing on per-instance geometric and material properties rather than view or frame-level state.
*   **Output:** A 32-byte binary blob suitable for GPU buffer binding (e.g., `GL_ARRAY_BUFFER` or `GL_SHADER_STORAGE_BUFFER`).
*   `up` is an enum value representing the primary axis direction (mapped to integer indices).
*   `forward` is an integer in the range $[0, 3]$ representing clockwise rotation perpendicular to the `up` axis.
Although the constructor may accept an `int`, values exceeding 65535 will wrap or truncate, causing incorrect shape assignment.
If the compiler or GPU driver inserts padding (e.g., default pack alignment), the offsets will be incorrect.
Explicit layout directives must be enforced on the CPU side.
Calculated as 19 floats ($19 \times 4 = 76$ bytes) + 1 int (4 bytes).
Vector3 uses 3 floats, Vector2 uses 2 floats.
Very compact, allowing high instance counts within GPU memory limits.
The combined `shapeRotation` uint allows for efficient bit-field extraction in shaders.
*   **Limitations:** The 16-bit shape ID limit (65,535 shapes) may be insufficient for highly complex scenes requiring many distinct voxel shapes.
The rotation encoding is limited to 12 discrete orientations (3 up directions $\times$ 4 forward rotations), which may not support arbitrary continuous rotation without additional data.
It was designed to efficiently pass instance data to the GPU for rendering voxel-based shapes using instanced rendering techniques.
The explicit packing ensures compatibility with OpenGL buffer objects.
